newsitem.title: USA: U.S. pipeline troubles trigger Eugene Island rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. pipeline troubles trigger Eugene Island rally.

text.p: U.S. cash crude markets featured a rallying Eugene Island sour business Monday morning following the shutdown of a Texaco pipeline after a spill.

June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing hovered around 20 cents cheaper at $21.85-95 a barrel, consolidating gains made last week. June/July spreads widened to a 20-25 cents advantage for second month July.
NYMEX June futures expire after the close of Tuesday business, setting the stage for paper market fluctuations.
Traders said Eugene Island barrels attracted deals at WTI/Cushing -$1.40, after starting the week at a $1.60 discount. Current talked ranged around a $1.45-50 discount.
Texaco said its 176,000 barrels per day (bpd) Eugene Island pipeline was shut in since Friday evening after a split in the pipeline caused a spill into Lake Barre in Louisiana.
About 20,000 bpd of the crude has been diverted to the Poseidon pipeline system, also owned by Texaco.
Other domestic grade talked had Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James bid around a one cents discount to June WTI/Cushing, and offered a few cents higher.
West Texas Sour/Midland was pegged at a $1.40 discount, steady from Friday. June WTI/Cushing Postings were at $1.98.
